ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the external auditory canal

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral hearing loss with aural fullness and otorrhea
salient_findings: Polypoid mass in the right external auditory canal
Right profound sensorineural hearing loss on pure-tone audiometry
key_facts: 4-year history of right aural fullness
Initial right middle ear effusion
No improvement with intranasal steroids and antihistamines
Myringotomy with insertion of a pressure-equalizing tube was performed
Painless right otorrhea developed 4 months prior to evaluation
Sensation that the right ear was shallower than the left
Polypoid mass occluded the right external auditory canal
Purulent discharge in the right external auditory canal
Right tympanic membrane not visualized
Left ear and facial nerve function were normal
High-resolution CT showed an irregularly enhancing mass in the right ear canal, middle ear cavity, and mastoid air cells

raw.rationale: The patient's history of chronic ear symptoms, including aural fullness and otorrhea, along with the presence of a polypoid mass and erosive changes of the skull base on CT, are consistent with a cholesteatoma. The lack of pain and the gradual progression of symptoms also support this diagnosis.
